text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Macedonian National Bank Governor Borko Stanoevski said in parliament that the MNB is not the only party responsible for the collapse of the Bitola-based financial institution TAT. He said his resignation was a moral act, but added that he was not involved in any criminal dealings.
- Deputy Prime Minister Ljube Trpevski denied in parliament any government involvement in the TAT affair.

- The surprise visit to Macedonia by Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos is a significant step forward in the relations of the two countries, which agree that existing borders should be preserved. "Albania brought Greece and Macedonia together," comments the daily.

- "If the Macedonian government does not allow the imports of 40 tonnes of flour to the Albanian border town of Peskopea, a massive exodus of Albanian refugees to Macedonia can be expected," a Peskopea local civil defence official has told the mayor of the town of Debar, western Macedonia. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom + 389 91 201 196
